notes: THE BUSINESS CHECKER (docs/history/1050): what a UK sole-trader tutoring business needs, in order. Guidance, not legal or financial advice. sense: an auto rule in js/biz-check.js (BC_RULES) or manual; renew: months or null; when: facts that must all hold (config biz_* keys). Links: gov.uk, ico.org.uk, nspcc.org.uk only (check-biz).

items.title: Register with HMRC as self-employed
items.why: You must tell HMRC by 5 October after the tax year you start, or face a penalty.
items.how: Register online for Self Assessment; you get a UTR (Unique Taxpayer Reference) in the post.

items.title: Open a separate business bank account
items.why: Keeping business money apart makes your records and tax return far easier.
items.how: Any high-street or online bank; note the bank under Business records.

items.title: Keep records of every payment in and out
items.why: HMRC can ask to see records for at least 5 years after the return deadline.
items.how: Keep receipts, invoices and bank statements; this site keeps a receipt for every booking.

items.title: Check your trading name is allowed
items.why: Some words need permission and you must not pass yourself off as another business.
items.how: Check the rules for sole trader names and put your own name on paperwork.

items.title: File your Self Assessment tax return
items.why: Online returns are due by 31 January after the tax year ends; late filing is fined.
items.how: File online with your UTR; pay any tax by the same date.

items.title: Plan for payments on account
items.why: Once your tax bill passes £1,000 HMRC asks for half of next year's tax in advance.
items.how: Put aside a share of every payment; dates are 31 January and 31 July.

items.title: Watch the VAT registration threshold
items.why: You must register within 30 days once 12 months' turnover passes the threshold.
items.how: Check the current threshold on gov.uk and set vat_threshold in config; this list warns as you near it.

items.title: Track income against your £100k goal
items.why: Knowing the weekly number keeps the goal real.
items.how: Bookings on this site are counted automatically from 6 April each tax year.

items.title: Get public liability insurance
items.why: Covers you if a learner or family is injured or their property damaged during a lesson.
items.how: Get quotes from insurers that cover tutors; record the policy under Business records.

items.title: Get professional indemnity insurance
items.why: Covers claims that your teaching or advice caused someone a loss.
items.how: Often sold together with public liability for tutors; record the renewal date.

items.title: Check insurance covers home visits and online lessons
items.why: Policies can exclude lessons in clients' homes or over video.
items.how: Ask your insurer in writing and keep the answer with the policy.

items.title: Pay the ICO data protection fee
items.why: Most businesses holding personal data must pay it every year or be fined.
items.how: Use the ICO self-assessment; the fee is renewed yearly.

items.title: Publish a privacy notice
items.why: People must be told what data you hold, why and for how long; children in words they understand.
items.how: Write one for families, learners and tutors and link it from the site.

items.title: Know what to do if data is lost
items.why: Serious breaches must be reported to the ICO within 72 hours.
items.how: Write a one-page plan: who decides, who is told, how it is logged.

items.title: Handle children's data with extra care
items.why: Under-18s get extra protection; photos and recordings need consent.
items.how: Collect only what lessons need; get a parent's consent for under-13s online.

items.title: Write a safeguarding policy
items.why: Anyone teaching children needs a written policy that tutors and parents can read.
items.how: Use the government guidance for tuition providers and the NSPCC template; review yearly.

items.title: Name a designated safeguarding lead
items.why: Someone must be the person concerns go to, with a deputy when they are away.
items.how: Usually you at first; put their name and number in the policy.

items.title: Get an enhanced DBS check for yourself
items.why: Families and councils expect the owner to be checked too.
items.how: Apply through an umbrella body, then join the DBS Update Service to keep it current.

items.title: Enhanced DBS for every tutor who teaches children
items.why: A tutor working alone with children must be checked, including the barred list.
items.how: Tick the DBS box on each tutor's record; ask them to join the Update Service.

items.title: Safeguarding training for you and your tutors
items.why: Training means people spot and report concerns properly.
items.how: Take a recognised course and refresh it every 2 to 3 years.

items.title: Set online-safety rules for video lessons
items.why: Online lessons with children need clear rules about platforms, recording and contact.
items.how: Lessons on business accounts only, parent nearby for young learners, no private messaging.

items.title: Set rules for lessons in families' homes
items.why: Home visits need an adult present and a way to report concerns.
items.how: A parent or carer stays in the home; tutors never take children elsewhere.

items.title: Extra care for under-8s
items.why: The youngest learners need a parent present and shorter, supervised sessions.
items.how: A parent or carer stays in the room for every under-8 lesson.

items.title: Check your tutors really are self-employed
items.why: If they work like employees, HMRC can ask you for tax and National Insurance.
items.how: Run the HMRC employment status tool for a typical tutor and keep the result.

items.title: Every tutor signs the tutor agreement
items.why: A written agreement shows the self-employed terms and the safeguarding rules.
items.how: Tutors agree in their Staff hub; this list ticks once every tutor has.

items.title: Safer recruitment for every new tutor
items.why: Checks before someone starts keep unsuitable people away from children.
items.how: Interview, check ID, qualifications and right to work, and get two references.

items.title: Take up two references for each tutor
items.why: References catch what an interview misses.
items.how: Ask referees directly, not through the tutor, and note the answers.

items.title: Onboard each tutor the same way
items.why: The same steps every time means nothing is missed as you grow.
items.how: Agreement, DBS, training, policy read, a first lesson observed.

items.title: Keep enough checked tutors for the work
items.why: Growing to £100k needs more tutors with every check done.
items.how: Listed tutors are counted from the site.

items.title: Publish terms and conditions for families
items.why: Clear terms prevent disputes about payment, lateness and missed lessons.
items.how: Say what you provide, prices, how to pay and how either side can end it.

items.title: Publish a cancellation and refund policy
items.why: Online bookings usually carry a 14-day right to cancel.
items.how: State notice needed, what is refunded and how; follow the distance-selling rules.

items.title: Have a simple complaints process
items.why: Families need to know how to complain and how fast you answer.
items.how: Name who handles it, how long you take and what happens next.

items.title: Make lessons and the site accessible
items.why: You must make reasonable adjustments for disabled learners.
items.how: Ask about needs at booking; check the site works with large text and screen readers.

items.title: Check if a venue needs Ofsted registration
items.why: Care for under-8s for more than 2 hours a day can need the Early Years or Childcare Register.
items.how: Read the Ofsted rules before opening; some tuition is exempt, check yours.

items.title: Do a written risk assessment for the venue
items.why: You must identify and reduce risks to children, staff and visitors.
items.how: Walk the space, write down hazards and what you do about each; review yearly.

items.title: Do a fire risk assessment
items.why: Anyone responsible for premises must assess fire risk.
items.how: Exits, alarms, extinguishers, a plan, and a drill.

items.title: First aid kit and a trained first aider
items.why: Children at a venue need someone who can help at once.
items.how: Keep a stocked kit and train at least one person on site.

items.title: Insure the venue
items.why: Buildings, contents and visitors need their own cover.
items.how: Tell your insurer about the venue and children on site.

items.title: Register as an employer for PAYE
items.why: You must register before the first payday.
items.how: Register with HMRC and run payroll every time you pay staff.

items.title: Auto-enrol staff in a workplace pension
items.why: Employers must enrol eligible staff and pay in.
items.how: Pick a scheme and tell The Pensions Regulator you have done it.

items.title: Get employers' liability insurance
items.why: It is a legal requirement once you employ anyone.
items.how: Display the certificate; record the renewal under Business records.

items.title: Give each employee a written contract
items.why: Employees must have written terms from their first day.
items.how: Use the gov.uk checklist for what a written statement must include.

items.title: Check every employee's right to work
items.why: Hiring someone without the right to work can bring a large fine.
items.how: Check and copy documents before they start.

items.title: Pay at least the minimum wage
items.why: Rates rise every April.
items.how: Check the current rates on gov.uk each spring.

items.title: Consider a limited company when profitable
items.why: A company can change your tax and protect personal assets; it adds paperwork.
items.how: Read the gov.uk guide and talk to an accountant before deciding.
